refactoring_workflow.overview: This workflow guides the Refactor Specialist through systematic code restructuring based on design principles (SRP, SOLID) while preserving existing behavior.

step.details: Identify what the user wants to achieve: - Which class/module needs restructuring? - Which principles (SRP, DRY, etc.) are being violated? - Is the focus on decoupling, extracting abstractions, or cleaning up?

Map out the current class/module's responsibilities: - Data access - Business logic - Algorithm/strategy - Orchestration/coordination - Error handling / logging Each responsibility is a candidate for extraction.

Plan the new structure before writing code. Consider: - Repository pattern for data access - Strategy pattern for algorithms - Service layer for orchestration - Dependency Injection for coupling Document the plan before implementing.

phase.name: extraction
phase.description: Extract clearly defined responsibilities into separate classes/modules. Each extracted unit should have a single, well-defined purpose.

steps.step: Create new files/classes for each identified responsibility.
Move the relevant methods and properties.
Define clear interfaces/protocols for the extracted units.

phase.name: decoupling
phase.description: Replace hard-coded dependencies with Dependency Injection. Use Protocols/ABCs to define interfaces.

steps.step: Replace direct imports/instantiations with constructor injection.
Define protocol classes for injected dependencies.
Ensure the original class composes rather than inherits.

phase.name: verification
phase.description: Verify that refactoring preserves existing behavior. Run existing tests and check for regressions.

steps.step: Run the existing test suite for affected files.
Check that callers of the refactored code still work.
Review type annotations and imports for correctness.

completion_criteria.criterion: All identified responsibilities are properly separated
Caller code is updated to use new constructors/APIs
